The invitation service emits the event but does not send the email itself.

I need to check withAction, getSessionPrincipal, login, insertMember, and seat limits. I also need to review inviteMemberSchema and verify whether emails are composed with tokens.

The plaintext invite token is never persisted. It is discarded after the hash is stored, and the invitation service does not pass it to sendEmail. The InviteEmail component exists for the accept URL, but nothing in the invitation service actually calls renderEmail or sendEmail.

Reviewing session principal and login logic. Checking seat limits, event bus emits, and organization scope assertions.

Also reviewing the invitations page and email mentions in invitation service comments. The full invite flow is now clear: admin submits an email, client validates schema and seat limits, server action hashes the token, stores it, discards the raw value, emits an event, and records activity.
Checking the event registry to see what gets registered at startup.

content.thinking: Checking whether seat usage counts pending invitations or only active usage.

I have a complete narrative. I will write concrete prose in order of execution.

Accept does not compare the session user's email to the invitation email. The existing member short-circuit returns the member without marking the invitation accepted or emitting a joined event. Seat recheck after insert can throw PlanLimitError even though the membership row already exists, so the form shows a seat error. Rate limiting is double-checked: the action consumes one token and the service consumes another for the batch length, and both must pass. UI checks are not the enforcement.

content.text:
An admin invite starts on the members settings page and ends as an active membership row. The raw token is the only credential in the accept link. The database stores a hash of it, and acceptance is what tells the rest of the system that a person has joined.

## Creating the invitation

On `src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/settings/members/page.tsx`, `loadTenantContext` resolves the org and the signed-in `Actor`. The page calls `can(actor, "member:read", …)` and returns `notFound()` if that fails. It then calls `can(actor, "member:invite", …)`, `listMembers`, and `checkLimit(org.id, "seats")` from `src/server/services/billing-service.ts`. `checkLimit` reads the subscription plan and the cached `usage.seatsUsed` counter. `getPlanLimits` supplies the seat ceiling shown next to that count. Only when `mayInvite` is true does the page render `InviteMemberForm` with `onSubmit={inviteMemberAction}`.

`InviteMemberForm` in `src/components/domain/member/invite-member-form.tsx` hides itself when `can(actor, "member:invite", organizationResource(orgId))` is false, and it disables a useful submit when `seatCheck.exceeded` or `seatCheck.remaining <= 0`. On submit it runs `inviteMemberSchema` (`src/schemas/member.ts`): a branded `orgId`, an email, and an `invitableRoleSchema` role (`admin`, `member`, or `viewer` — never `owner`), with an optional message of at most 500 characters. Those UI checks are not the enforcement.

`inviteMemberAction` in `src/actions/members/invite-member.ts` goes through `withAction` (`src/actions/_lib/with-action.ts`), which parses the same schema, resolves an `Actor` with `requireActorFor(orgId)`, and later maps thrown errors with `toActionResult`. Inside the handler, in order:

1. `can(actor, "member:invite", …)` against a pending-member resource. `ROLE_MATRIX` in `src/lib/permissions.ts` requires `admin`. A cross-tenant actor is denied. Failure throws `ForbiddenActionError`.
2. `consumeRateLimit(orgId, "member:invite")` (`src/lib/rate-limit.ts`). The base bucket is capacity 20, refill 2 per minute, scaled by the org plan. Failure throws `RateLimitedError`.
3. `getOrganizationSummary` plus `getPlanLimits`. If `seatsUsed + 1` exceeds `limits.seats`, it throws `PlanLimitError`. This counter is the cached usage number, not a live count of pending invites.
4. `inviteMember(actor, input)`.

`inviteMember` in `src/server/services/invitation-service.ts` delegates to `inviteMembers` with a one-element batch. That function checks again, in this order:

1. `assertOrgScope(actor, input.orgId)` (`src/lib/tenant.ts`).
2. `assertCan(actor, "member:invite", orgResource(orgId))`.
3. `consumeRateLimit` a second time, with cost equal to the batch size. A single invite from the settings page therefore spends two tokens.
4. `findOrgById`. Seat usage is `countActiveMembers(orgId)` (status `active`, not soft-deleted) plus `countPendingInvitations(orgId)` (rows whose `acceptedAt` and `revokedAt` are both null, including expired rows). `wouldExceedLimit(org.plan, "seats", seatsUsed, batchLength)` rejects the whole batch if one more seat would pass the plan ceiling.

For each address, `randomToken(32)` in `src/lib/hash.ts` draws 32 random bytes and encodes them as base64url. `hashToken` stores only `sha256(token)` as hex. `insertInvitation` (`src/server/repositories/invitation-repository.ts`) writes the `invitations` row defined in `src/server/db/schema/members.ts`: new id, `orgId`, email, role, `invitedBy` (the actor's user id), `tokenHash`, `expiresAt` (now plus `expiresInDays`, fixed at 14 by the service), `acceptedAt` and `revokedAt` null, and timestamps. A unique index is on `token_hash`. The plaintext token is not a column, and it is not part of the `member.invited` payload. After the insert it is dropped.

`emit("member.invited", { orgId, actorId, occurredAt, email, role })` runs on the in-process bus (`src/lib/event-bus.ts`). Handlers are attached from `registerEventHandlers` in `src/server/services/event-registry.ts`. The activity listener in `registerActivityListeners` (`src/server/services/activity-service.ts`) records a `member.invited` activity whose subject is the email and whose summary is `Invited {email} as {role}`. Nothing in this path calls `renderEmail` or `sendEmail`. `InviteEmail` (`src/emails/invite-email.tsx`) is the template that would carry `acceptUrl`, and `sendEmail` only writes a log line, but `inviteMembers` never builds that URL or sends that mail.

The action then calls `revalidateTagged` for the org and the `members` and `invitations` tags.

## What the link carries

The accept route is `src/app/(auth)/invite/[token]/page.tsx`. The credential in the URL is the raw base64url token. `src/proxy.ts` treats every `/invite` path as public, so a missing session cookie does not bounce the request before the page runs. The page itself only checks the shape with `invitationTokenSchema` (`src/schemas/invitation.ts`): 32 to 128 characters matching `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$`. It does not look the token up. A bad shape renders "This invitation is not valid". A visitor with no session (`getSessionPrincipal()` in `src/lib/session.ts` is null) is redirected to `/login?next=/invite/{token}`. A signed-in visitor sees `InviteAcceptForm`, which posts the token back. An optional `?org=` query value is only a slug used for the redirect after success. It is not stored and it is not checked.

## Using the link

`InviteAcceptForm` (`src/app/(auth)/invite/[token]/invite-accept-form.tsx`) calls `acceptInvitationAction({ token })`. That action (`src/actions/members/accept-invitation.ts`) does not use `withAction`, because the user is not yet a member and there is no `Actor`. It parses `acceptInvitationTokenSchema`, then `getSessionPrincipal()`. No session throws `UnauthorizedActionError` ("Sign in before accepting an invitation."). It does not compare the session email to `invitation.email`.

`acceptInvitation(userId, { token })` then:

1. `findInvitationByTokenHash(hashToken(token))`. This is the one repository read that is not filtered by `orgId`. The hash is the lookup key, and the row carries the tenant. A miss throws not-found.
2. Rejects the row when `revokedAt` is set, when `acceptedAt` is set, or when `expiresAt` is less than or equal to the current ISO timestamp.
3. `findMember(orgId, userId)`. If that user is already a member, it returns that row and does not mark the invitation accepted and does not emit `member.joined`.
4. Otherwise `insertMember` (`src/server/repositories/member-repository.ts`) inserts a `members` row: new id, `orgId`, `userId`, the invitation's role, `status: "active"`, `invitedBy` copied from the invitation, `joinedAt` set to now.
5. `markInvitationAccepted` sets `acceptedAt` and `updatedAt`.
6. `emit("member.joined", { orgId, actorId: userId, occurredAt, memberId, userId, role })`.

Back in the action, `assertSeatAvailable` runs only after that insert. It calls `resolveActor(userId, orgId)`, then `getOrganizationSummary`, then `getPlanLimits`. If `usage.seatsUsed` is already above `limits.seats`, it throws `PlanLimitError`. The membership row is already written at that point. The form shows the seat-limit message when the error code is `plan_limit_exceeded`. On success it navigates to `/{orgSlug}` when the page had `?org=`, otherwise to `/orgs`.

## What the rest of the system learns

`member.joined` is what fans out. `registerUsageListeners` in `src/server/services/usage-service.ts` increments `seatsUsed` by 1. That cached counter is what the members page and `checkLimit` read. Pending invitations do not move it. They only occupy a seat inside `inviteMembers`'s live count of active members plus pending rows. The notification fan-out in `src/server/services/notification-service.ts` loads the org and calls `notify(orgId, "member_joined", [org.ownerId], …)` with a link to `/settings/members`. The activity registry has a label for `member.joined`, but `registerActivityListeners` does not subscribe to it. `registerWebhookListeners` does not dispatch it either, even though `src/schemas/webhook.ts` lists the event name. Search indexing is not subscribed to it. Revoking or resending is a separate admin path: `revokeInvitation` sets `revokedAt`, and `resendInvitation` revokes the old row and calls `inviteMember` again so the previous link stops matching.
